newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-BRITAIN WANTS REPORT ON PORTO TROUBLE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BRITAIN WANTS REPORT ON PORTO TROUBLE.

text.p: Britain said on Thursday it was urgently seeking a report from Portugal after eight Manchester United soccer fans were injured when police opened fire with anti-riot pellets after a European Cup match against Porto.
"We are urgently seeking a police report from the Portuguese authorities," a British Foreign Office spokesman said in London.

Eight United fans were taken to Oporto's main hospital with pellet wounds after Wednesday's quarter-final, but all were discharged in the early hours of Thursday, a British Embassy spokeswoman in the city said.
"They have all left (hospital)," Marilia Astle said. She said that there was only one Briton still being treated but that was for a case of dehydration.

Some 20 other English fans were also slightly hurt in the clashes in which police used batons and threw smoke grenades when some United fans tried to leave the ground before the end of the game, ignoring an order to stay put.
Authorities at Porto's As Antas stadium had told United fans, totalling some 10,000, to remain in the ground at the end of the match to allow local supporters to leave first as a security precaution.
It was not immediately known why a number of fans ignored the call, but when they tried to force one of the exit doors, they were driven back by police.
"It was a disgrace, they opened fire on us. I have five wounds," one United fan said.
A police spokesman said that some 15 police officials were also hurt in the incident.
The match ended 0-0 but Manchester United went through 4-0 on aggregate after trouncing Porto in the first leg at Old Trafford.

There had also been trouble involving United supporters at the start of the game. Some 20 English fans were hurt -- most of them with cuts and bruises -- after a group with no valid tickets sought to force their way into the ground. They were eventually allowed in to see the game.
